parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Complete the equation to show the decay of plutonium-238.

$$^{238}_{94}\mathrm{Pu} \to {}^{\text{........}}_{\text{........}}\mathrm{U} + {}^{\text{........}}_{\text{........}}\alpha$$

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem: The power source in a space probe contains $0.874\,\text{kg}$ of plutonium-238. Each nucleus of plutonium-238 that decays emits $5.59\,\text{MeV}$ of energy. The half-life of plutonium-238 is $87.7\,\text{years}$.
parts.text:
Calculate the initial number $N_{0}$ of nuclei of plutonium-238 in the power source.

$$N_{0} = \text{....................................................}$$

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Determine the initial activity of the source. Give a unit with your answer.

$$\text{activity} = \text{....................................................}\,\text{unit} = \text{..........................}$$

(Bq)

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
Use your answer in (b)(ii) to determine the initial power output from the source due to the decay of plutonium-238.

$$\text{power output} = \text{....................................................}\,\mathrm{W}$$

(W)

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text:
The space probe will continue to function until the power output from the plutonium in the source decreases to $65.3\%$ of its initial value.
Calculate the time, in years, for which the space probe will function.

$$\text{time} = \text{....................................................}\,\text{years}$$

(years)

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
An alternative power source uses energy generated from the radioactive decay of polonium-210. This isotope has a half-life of $0.378\,\text{years}$. The mass of the isotope needed for the same initial power output as in (b) is $3.37\,\mathrm{g}$.
Suggest one advantage and one disadvantage of using polonium-210 as the source of energy.

stem: Plutonium-238 (^{238}_{94}Pu) is unstable and undergoes alpha decay.
